_note: Sources for Form 2 Home Economics (Batches H2-1, H2-2 and H2-3, Terms 1–3). The answers are authored facts: a Home Economics teacher must check them.

nutrients.ref: Nutrition as taught in Cameroonian Home Economics (food science): classes of nutrients, composition, sources, functions, deficiencies, effects of heat; vitamins and minerals; dietary fibre (NSP)
nutrients.supports: Macronutrients and micronutrients; marasmus and kwashiorkor; gelatinisation, dextrinisation, caramelisation, coagulation; fat-soluble and water-soluble vitamins; iron, calcium, iodine, sodium, fluoride; hidden hunger; fibre sources and functions.
nutrients.checked: Standard textbook content, not externally sourced in this session: please check the examples and deficiency names.

food-energy.ref: Energy values of the macronutrients: carbohydrate and protein 4 kcal (17 kJ) per gram, fat 9 kcal (37 kJ) per gram
food-energy.checked: Standard values; totals computed by code.

water-health.ref: Water in nutrition; water-borne diseases and their prevention (WHO water, sanitation and hygiene guidance)
water-health.supports: Sources and functions of water; dehydration; cholera, typhoid, dysentery, hepatitis A, bilharzia; ORS; boiling, filtering, chlorination, latrines, handwashing.
water-health.checked: General knowledge, not opened in this session: please check.

kitchens.ref: Traditional and modern kitchens, as in Form One Home Economics (TR-H01, TR-H02)
kitchens.supports: Traditional kitchen items, fuels and fireplaces; advantages, disadvantages and care; modern kitchen shapes, units, the work triangle (sides 1.2–2.7 m, total 4–7.9 m), planning points, time management and care. The drawings are the Form One ones (homeeconomics.js).
kitchens.checked: Work-triangle rule and drawings as approved for Form One review; other items authored: please check.

kitchen-equipment.ref: Small and large kitchen equipment: types, parts, uses, choice and care (as in Cameroonian Form 2 home economics)
kitchen-equipment.supports: Groups of small tools, materials, parts of a knife and saucepan; cooker, fridge (0–5 °C), freezer (about −18 °C), dishwasher; points of choice and care.
kitchen-equipment.checked: Standard textbook content: please check. The diagram lessons (rows 24, 27, 29) use described parts, not drawings.

labour-saving.ref: Labour-saving equipment: microwave oven, pressure cooker, blender, mixer, vacuum flask; parts, principles, choice and care
labour-saving.supports: Pressure raises the boiling point (about 120 °C); microwaves heat water in food; the vacuum flask stops conduction and convection and reflects radiation; fill a pressure cooker no more than two-thirds; mains 220 V.
labour-saving.checked: Standard physics and textbook content: please check.

kitchen-safety.ref: Kitchen accidents: types, causes, prevention and first aid
kitchen-safety.supports: Burns, scalds, cuts, falls, shocks, fires, poisoning; cool a burn under running water for about 20 minutes; cover burning oil, never water.
kitchen-safety.checked: Standard first-aid advice: please check with current first-aid guidance.

kitchen-waste.ref: Kitchen waste: types, generation and sorting
kitchen-waste.supports: Food, packaging, liquid and other waste; sorting at the source; reducing waste.

cooking-methods.ref: Reasons for cooking; moist and dry methods, their advantages and disadvantages
cooking-methods.supports: Boiling, simmering, stewing, steaming, poaching, braising; baking, roasting, grilling, toasting, shallow and deep frying.

heat-transfer.ref: Heat transfer in cooking: conduction, convection, radiation
heat-transfer.supports: Good and poor conductors; convection currents; dull black and shiny surfaces; kitchen examples.

deficiency-diseases.ref: Kwashiorkor, marasmus and night blindness: causes, signs, children at risk, prevention
deficiency-diseases.supports: Protein and energy deficiency signs; exclusive breastfeeding for six months; enriched weaning foods; vitamin A sources (red palm oil, carrots, mango, pawpaw, green leaves, liver, eggs).
deficiency-diseases.checked: Standard nutrition content (WHO advice on breastfeeding): please check.

embroidery.ref: Embroidery: traditional (toghu, Bamoun, Fulani designs) and modern; stitches (running, back, straight, satin, zigzag, chain, blanket); fabrics (cotton, linen, silk, wool, synthetics); counted-thread (cross stitch, Aida cloth); white work, candlewicking, shadow work; tools
embroidery.checked: Standard needlework content: please check the local design names.

laundry.ref: Clothing labels and care symbols (tub, triangle, square, iron with dots, circle); types of laundry (home, on-premises, commercial); types of irons (charcoal, dry, steam, steam generator, automatic); ironing technique
